text: We are focusing on the important questions concerning the locus and nature of verbal satiation produced by the discounting mechanism of information. There are three divergent theoretical descriptions that answer these questions: (1) The term semantic satiation emphasizes the locus of verbal satiation is thought to be semantic ( Lambert and Jakobovits, 1960 ; Smith and Klein, 1990 ; Pynte, 1991 ; Black, 2001 ); (2) The term lexical satiation makes a point that the “loss of meaning” is dependent upon the changes in the processing of the orthographic or the phonological representation of the word ( Esposito and Pelton, 1971 ; Tian and Huber, 2010 ); (3) Associative satiation states that the less efficient association between the lexical representation entry and its associated meaning results in the verbal satiation ( Tian and Huber, 2010 ; Yuan et al., 2017 ).
source_label: A Lexical Representational Mechanism Underlying Verbal Satiation: An Empirical Study With Rarely Used Chinese Characters
